Subject: Post-discovery: schedule technical deep dive (ML/Infra)

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a proposal for next steps: we recommend a 60–90 minute technical deep dive with your ML and infra teams to align on architecture, integration points, and performance targets. The goals of the session would be:

- Walk through NovaHealth's current ML inference architecture and latency/cost constraints
- Share Redwood's serving/runtime approach and deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private)
- Define performance targets, integration requirements, and test data/access needs
- Identify success criteria and immediate next steps (PoC scope, timeline)

Proposed time slots (all PT):
- Tue Mar 27: 10:00–11:00 or 10:30–11:30
- Wed Mar 28: 14:00–15:30 (60–90m)
- Thu Mar 29: 09:00–10:30

Please confirm which slot works and who from your side will join (ideally ML lead + infra/SRE). I've attached a short run-of-show agenda for the session (redwood_technical_deep_dive_agenda.pdf).

Pre-call ask: if you can share the expected QPS/latency targets and a sanitized sample of request shapes (or a quick description of sequence lengths / typical batch sizes), that’ll help our engineers come prepared.

Thanks — happy to sync on any of the proposed times.

Best,
Camila Reyes

1) 5–10m — Introductions & objectives (Camila / Sanjay)
2) 15–20m — NovaHealth current architecture + pain points (Elena / Miguel)
3) 20–25m — Redwood serving/runtime overview and deployment options (Marissa / Camila)
4) 20–30m — Integration considerations, data flow, and access patterns (engineering breakout if needed)
5) 10–15m — Performance targets, testing plan, and next steps

Pre-call checklist (please send before Tue Mar 27 EOD if possible):
- Brief architecture diagram or bullet list of components handling inference
- Expected traffic profile (QPS / burst patterns), average & max sequence lengths

Looking forward to it. If anything changes on timing or attendees, let me know and I’ll update the invite.
